body.statement:
Under the frozen definition of \(\mathfrak L_U(P_0)\), the requested uniform asymptotic-linear conclusion, and hence the requested four-part affirmative attainment result, is false in general. In particular, take \(P_0=P^{\star}\) and fixed margins that admit the witness with slack. For every sufficiently small nonzero \(\delta\), let \(Q_\delta\) retain the donor means and innovation laws of \(P^{\star}\) but replace the treated untreated mean path by \((-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta)\), and define
\[
 \Delta_\delta
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})
  -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star}).
\]
Then \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]\ge\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
\]
For every sample size, finite-coordinate splicing produces two elements of \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\) having the same observed law at that coordinate but different admissible chart labels. No single estimator can have both chart expansions uniformly. The assumptions permit sequencewise local claims only; a genuine uniform theorem requires a common local neighborhood, a common bound on the QMD scores and remainders, and exclusion of arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.
body.proof_tex:
The obstruction comes from the quantifiers in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}union\text{-}sequences}\), not from failure of the center QP. Choose the fixed margins so that \(P^{\star}\) satisfies the moment, rank, spectral-gap, overlap, and variance conditions with strict slack. For a fixed sufficiently small \(\delta\ne0\), retain the donor means and all innovation laws of \(P^{\star}\), and replace the treated untreated mean path by
\[
 (1/2+\delta)(-1,-2,-2)+(1/2-\delta)(1,2,2)
 =(-2\delta,-4\delta,-4\delta).
 \tag{1}
\]
Give its treated final outcome the same fixed additive treatment effect as under \(P^{\star}\), and call the resulting law \(Q_\delta\). Both donor changes and the treated untreated change remain zero, so the parallel-trends assumption holds. Equation (1) is reproduced by the unique full-rank SC weights \((1/2+\delta,1/2-\delta)\), so the synthetic-mean assumption also holds. The group probabilities stay equal to \(1/3\), and the innovations stay bounded. By continuity of the finite Gram matrices, their nonzero eigenvalues, and the local-score variance, all strict support, moment, rank, spectral-gap, and variance margins continue to hold for sufficiently small \(|\delta|\). Thus \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\) and it satisfies every coordinatewise margin in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}local\text{-}union\text{-}sequences}\).

Fix an integer \(m\). Form two triangular sequences. In each sequence, set the law at index \(m\) equal to \(Q_\delta\) and the law at every other index equal to \(P^{\star}\). Give the \(m\)-th coordinate label PT in the first sequence and SC in the second; use any admissible label at every other coordinate. Each sequence belongs to \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\): after its one exceptional coordinate it is identically \(P^{\star}\), so the QMD equation holds eventually with score zero and remainder zero, and every coordinate satisfies the fixed margins. Therefore, when a supremum is taken over all sequences separately at each sample size \(m\), its \(m\)-th coordinate contains both labeled copies of the same law \(Q_\delta\). This is the finite-coordinate-splicing defect.

By Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}strict\text{-}three\text{-}group\text{-}witness}\), the common score at \(P^{\star}\) uses final donor weights \((1/2,1/2)\). Hence the PT chart extension, whose normal coefficient is frozen at \(P^{\star}\), still has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\) at \(Q_\delta\). An SC normal has only preperiod coordinates, whereas the unrestricted SC gradient at \(Q_\delta\) has final donor coefficients \((-1/2-\delta,-1/2+\delta)\). Thus, for
\[
 \Delta_\delta(O)
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})(O)
  -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star})(O),
\]
the final-innovation component is \(\delta(z_{2,3}-z_{3,3})\). The remaining components involve innovations at other group-period coordinates. Independence of all innovations makes those components orthogonal to the final component. The variance list (3) in the witness proof gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 &\ge \delta^2\{\operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{2,3})
                  +\operatorname{Var}_{Q_\delta}(z_{3,3})\}\\
 &=\delta^2\left(\frac32+6\right)
 =\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
Both chart extensions are mean-zero influence functions, so \(E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta]=0\).

Suppose, contrary to the claim, that one estimator had the requested asymptotic-linear expansion uniformly over the frozen sequence class and its admissible labels. Apply that expansion at sample size \(m\) to the two spliced sequences. Their left sides are identical because their \(m\)-th data law and their causal target are both the same \(Q_\delta\). Subtracting the two expansions would force
\[
 m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta_\delta(O_i)=o_{Q_\delta}(1)
 \tag{3}
\]
uniformly as \(m\to\infty\). By iid sampling and the preceding centering, the variance of the left side of (3) is exactly \(E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]\), which is bounded below by \((15/2)\delta^2\) for every \(m\). Moreover, \(\Delta_\delta\) is a bounded linear combination of the Rademacher innovations. The fourth moments of the normalized sums in (3) are therefore uniformly bounded. If (3) converged in probability to zero, uniform integrability of its squares would force its variance to converge to zero, contradicting (2).

Thus no estimator can satisfy the requested uniform asymptotic-linear expansion. Since that expansion is one conjunct of the proposed four-part construction, the full affirmative conclusion, including variance consistency and multiplier coverage tied to it, is impossible under the frozen class. The argument does not contradict the sequencewise chart continuation result: it shows precisely that a positive uniform theorem additionally needs a single uniformly quantified neighborhood, common bounds on QMD scores and remainders, and a ban on arbitrary finite-coordinate replacements.
